name: Geroch (1967) topology-change theorem, with Borde's causally compact generalisation (gr-qc/9406053, Theorem 1): kinematic, no T_ab or field-equation assumption; topology change forces a closed timelike curve

published_statement: Geroch as restated in 2505.02210 Thm III.2: 'Let W be a compact spacetime whose boundary is the disjoint union of two compact spacelike 3-manifolds, Sigma_i and Sigma_f. If W has no CTCs, then Sigma_i and Sigma_f are diffeomorphic, and, furthermore, W is topologically equivalent to Sigma_i x [0,1].' (Def. 6: a spacetime is a 4-manifold 'together with an everywhere non-degenerate time-orientable Lorentzian metric'.) Borde Theorem 1: 'Let M be a (time-oriented) causally compact spacetime that interpolates between an initial surface S1 and a final surface S2. Suppose that M has no closed timelike curves. Then, M is diffeomorphic to S1 x [0,1] (and, in particular, S1 is diffeomorphic to S2).' Borde: 'By "causality violation" it is meant that there is at least one closed timelike curve.' Borde sec. IX: 'Neither Geroch's original theorem, nor its mild generalization in section IV, assume anything about the energy-momentum tensor, or indeed about a field equation - the results are purely kinematical.'
published_hypotheses: M (W) is an interpolating manifold: connected, smooth, Hausdorff, paracompact, boundary = S1 u S2 (u T, a compact timelike tube, in Borde's generalisation) [Borde sec. II.A]

a smooth, EVERYWHERE NON-DEGENERATE Lorentz metric on all of M, with S1 and S2 spacelike (T timelike, with a timelike field tangent to T whose integral curves run S1 to S2) [Borde II.A; 2505.02210 Def. 6]
TIME-ORIENTED / time-orientable [Borde Thm 1 '(time-oriented)'; 2505.02210 Def. 6]. Borde sec. VII/IX: non-time-orientable metrics avoid the CTC only when one of the boundaries is empty

Geroch: W compact with compact (closed) spacelike boundary components (closed-universe case; Geroch also treats the externally Lorentzian case, per Borde). Borde: M causally compact (closure of I(p) compact for every p), which compact M satisfies trivially
Geroch as restated in 2505.02210: dimension 4 (3-manifold slices). Borde: no assumption on dimension for Theorem 1
NO energy condition, NO field equation, NO geodesic-completeness assumption
Conclusion is a CTC somewhere in M (the interpolating region); nothing locates it further

Borde's Thm 1 is for a '(time-oriented)' spacetime. COST HERE: small -- Borde sec. IX says non-time-orientable metrics avoid CTCs only when one boundary is empty, and a throat created inside an existing space has neither boundary empty. It would matter only for creation from nothing.

So, this might well prove to be the correct approach'). The tree's three escapes are IX.A, IX.B and the Euclidean path integral; Borde's own three 'within the general Lorentzian framework' are IX.A, IX.B, IX.C. So ledger.py:630-631 'one of Borde's three escapes, and none stays inside Lorentzian GR without a pathology' matches Borde's count but not his membership; it holds only if a degenerate point is counted a pathology, which the tree does not state (Borde notes curvature cannot be computed there and causal structure may be undefined). Relevant because M's own mechanism puts a singular throat at the creation site (M-S1A-P3, DOCKET 66).

WEAKENED (in the tree's favour) -- the inference 'SO EXOTIC MATTER CANNOT HELP' (create.py:60, create.py:340) and EXOTIC_MATTER_HELPS_CREATION = False (create.py:186; ledger.py:628-629; specthm.py:1148-1149; gate of fact GEROCH-BORDE specthm.py:1838-1841). What the theorem supports is narrower: exotic matter cannot REMOVE the forced CTC (z3 unsat in the re-derivation). It does not support 'cannot help creation': Borde IX.B names energy-condition violation as the route past his DYNAMICAL obstruction (Theorem 3's half-integral null convergence condition (ii)) -- 'there might be violations of the energy conditions large enough to allow assumption (ii) to be violated. Some discussions of wormhole creation are, for example, based precisely on large violations of the energy condition' -- while noting it 'would not affect the presence of causality violations'. create.ESCAPES[1] (create.py:215-217) carries only the other half of IX.B ('altering Einstein's equation ... fairly severe'). 2505.02210 then builds exactly that: a non-singular wormhole nucleation with CTCs that 'violates all the standard energy conditions'. The flag is right about the CTC and overreaches about creation.

NOT A DRIFT -- 'Geroch's closed-universe argument' (create.py:64) is Borde's abstract wording; specthm's 'ctc' literal (specthm.py:1844) matches Borde's definition of causality violation (at least one CTC); specthm's W-create-cc note (specthm.py:1654-1657) that the forced CTC 'lies in the interpolating region' matches the theorem. The four quoted constants BORDE, BORDE_SINGULARITY, BORDE_DYNAMICS, BORDE_CAUTION and the phrases 'only to be had at a price', 'a very wide range of situations', 'highly undesirable feature', 'fairly severe' all occur verbatim in the source (re-derivation part A).

SCOPE KEPT HONEST BY THE TREE -- D24 (ledger.py:626-627) and R10(e) restrict to 'CAUSALLY COMPACT INTERPOLATING SPACETIMES', and theorems_apply_to_enlargement() = False; both match the source. R10(e)'s 'whether reasonable excludes the source a throat needs is not determined here' is accurate: Borde's 'reasonable' is Theorem 3's conditions (i) generic and (ii) half-integral NCC, not the weak energy condition.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for THIS result. The theorem has no empirical input: Geroch (1967) and Borde (1994) used only the hypotheses listed (non-degenerate time-orientable Lorentz metric, spacelike boundaries, compactness / causal compactness); no measured quantity enters, so no later datum can move the conclusion. What came later is mathematical and framework-level, and all of it is consistent with the theorem: Borde widened the class (compact -> causally compact) and kept the conclusion; Gibbons-Hawking added selection rules; 2505.02210 (2025) constructed an explicit non-singular wormhole nucleation and found the CTC Geroch forces, exactly where the Misner connected sum puts it. Evidence AGAINST 'the authors lacked data and are therefore wrong' here: 58 years of use, two independent restatements agreeing verbatim in content, an explicit instance built in the re-derivation, and no counterexample within the hypotheses in anything read. Evidence FOR 'incomplete': the result is deliberately scoped -- its hypotheses (non-degenerate metric, time orientation, causal compactness, classical Lorentzian framework) are exactly what the later escapes relax (degenerate/Morse metrics, non-time-orientable creation from nothing, non-compact interpolation, Euclidean/quantum), and Borde himself says the theorems' 'true value' is to 'pinpoint what modifications we have to make'. That incompleteness is in the SCOPE, not in the data, and it is where the tree's use narrows (the dropped non-degeneracy hypothesis and the exotic-matter overreach).
grade_evidence: The kinematic theorem itself stands: every quotation the tree carries is verbatim in Borde (part A); Geroch's statement is restated consistently in 2505.02210 Thm III.2; Borde's own 2-D example is built with an explicit non-degenerate metric and exhibits the forced CTC and the proof's accumulation mechanism (part D); the proof's finite core and the Thm1/Thm3 logic pass z3 with vacuity guards (part F). No datum enters. The tree's USE is narrower than the source in three named places, none of which is a refutation: (1) time-orientability dropped (create.py:64-66, specthm.py:1146-1148, 1843; ledger.py:626-628) -- harmless unless a boundary is empty; (2) the non-degenerate-metric hypothesis dropped and Borde's escape IX.C 'Degenerate metrics' omitted from create.ESCAPES (create.py:211-220), so 'none stays inside Lorentzian GR without a pathology' (ledger.py:630-631) holds only if a degenerate point is counted a pathology -- which the tree does not state and which bears on M's singular-throat mechanism; (3) 'SO EXOTIC MATTER CANNOT HELP' / EXOTIC_MATTER_HELPS_CREATION = False (create.py:60, 186, 340; ledger.py:628-629; specthm.py:1148-1149, 1838-1841) is supported only as 'exotic matter cannot remove the forced CTC' (z3 unsat); Borde IX.B names large energy-condition violation as the route past the dynamical obstruction for wormhole creation, and 2505.02210 realises it (non-singular, CTCs, all ECs violated) -- z3: created & cc & Einstein & exotic is sat with ctc True. Under M-S1A-P3 (a CTC disqualifies at the seat only), that route is precisely the one left open, consistent with the tree's own OPEN verdict on W-create-cc.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree adds time-orientation and an everywhere non-degenerate Lorentz metric to H_cc / the GEROCH-BORDE fact, adds Borde IX.C (degenerate metrics) and the energy-condition half of IX.B to create.ESCAPES, and scopes EXOTIC_MATTER_HELPS_CREATION to 'cannot remove the forced CTC'. To WRONG: a time-oriented, causally compact interpolating spacetime with a smooth non-degenerate Lorentz metric, non-diffeomorphic spacelike boundaries and no CTC -- none exists in anything read, and Borde's proof and Geroch's rule it out. To OPEN on the source side: if the cached Borde / 2505.02210 texts proved not to be the arXiv versions (re-read at alphaXiv when the quota resets; Geroch 1967 itself remains NAMED-NOT-READ at source).
